title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC Ad 3–5 — Cain; first vs later; elect liberation
pass_a_gloss: To the third—why Adam's sin hurt Cain and Cain's not Adam: Adam begot Cain, not Cain Adam. To the fourth—why the first corrupted us more than later Adam-sins: the first corrupted Adam's nature; the later followed as effects of corruption already made. To the fifth—why Adam was freed from the corruption his act brought, and infants who did no evil are not: he was freed from its guilt by justifying grace and from inherent penalties by regenerating grace, because he believed and repented—and believed because he was elect. So with all the elect. Why this one rather than that is elect can be credited to no cause but God's freest will doing what He will with His own. He begot, not according to grace, but according to nature, conceiving corrupt ones—as one circumcised by art begets the uncircumcised.
pass_b_english: To the third: Why did Adam's sin hurt Cain, and Cain's sin hurt Adam not at all? Because Adam begot Cain, not Cain Adam. To the fourth: Why did the first sin rather corrupt us than Adam's following sins? Because that corrupted Adam's nature; those followed corruption already made as effects follow a cause. To the fifth: Why was Adam freed from that corruption which by his action he procured for himself, and all infants, who have done no evil, are not freed? He was freed from the guilt of that corruption by the grace of justification, and from the inherence of penalties by the grace of regeneration, because he believed and repented; and he believed because he was elect. The same happens to all other elect. But why this one rather than that was elect can be ascribed to no other cause than the freest will of God, who does what He will with His own. And he begot not according to grace, but according to nature, conceiving corrupt ones, just as one circumcised by art begets the uncircumcised.
source_text: Ad 3. Cur Adami peccatum Caino nocuit, Caini peccatum Adamo minime nocuit? quia Adamus genuit Cainum, non Cainus Adamum. Ad 4. Cur primum peccatum nos potius corrupit, quam sequentia Adami peccata? quia illud naturam Adami corrupit, ista corruptionem jam factam consequuta sunt ut causam effecta. Ad 5. Cur Adamus ab illa corruptione liberatus est, quam sua actione sibi comparavit; infantes omnes, qui nihil mali egerunt, non liberantur? Liberatus est ab illius corruptionis reatu gratia justificationis, & ab inhaerentia poenarum gratia regenerationis, quia credidit & resipuit; credidit autem, quia fuit electus. Idem evenit aliis omnibus electis. Cur autem hic potius quam ille fuerit electus, alii causae quam liberrimae Dei voluntati, de suo quod vult facientis, tribui nequit. Genuit autem non secundum gratiam, sed secundum naturam, conceptus corruptos, sicut arte circumcissus gignit incircumcisos.
